html:
The first set of Spanish laws on how colonists had to treat Indigenous people in the Americas, issued by King Ferdinand II at Burgos in 1512.

They came after the friar Antonio de Montesinos preached in Santo Domingo in 1511 that the colonists were in mortal sin for their cruelty to the Taíno. The colonists complained, and the king called a council of officials and theologians.

The 35 laws kept the encomienda, the system of forced Indigenous labour, but tried to soften it. Colonists had to feed and house their workers, teach them Christianity, and not beat them or call them dogs. Pregnant women were spared heavy work.

The laws were hardly enforced, and the Taíno population kept falling. Critics like Bartolomé de las Casas went on pressing the crown, which led to the stronger New Laws of 1542.
sum: The first set of Spanish laws on how colonists had to treat Indigenous people in the Americas, issued by King Ferdinand II at Burgos in 1512.
